jobs.description:
Mission

The South–North Laboratory for Sustainable Construction and Conservation (SONO Lab) at EPFL is recruiting a full-time PhD Student (100%) within the School of Architecture, Civil and Environmental Engineering (ENAC), based at the EPFL Fribourg associated campus.

SONO Lab investigates low-carbon, climate-responsive and socially inclusive approaches to building design, construction and conservation. Its research combines architectural design, environmental assessment, digital methods, full-scale experimentation, building-performance monitoring and participatory approaches, with a particular focus on collaborations between Europe and Africa.

The successful candidate will contribute to REGEN4BE—Regenerative Design for the Built Environment, a Horizon Europe project developed within the New European Bauhaus framework. REGEN4BE seeks to make regenerative design measurable, interoperable and scalable through digital tools, innovative materials, participatory processes, Living Labs and policy development. Its outputs include a Regenerative Evaluation Framework and the Regenerative Design Intelligence Platform (REDIP). Fribourg is one of the project’s European demonstration and replication sites.

Within REGEN4BE, the candidate will develop and scientifically validate interoperable digital workflows linking Building Information Modelling (BIM), Building Energy Modelling (BEM), Life-Cycle Assessment (LCA), embodied and operational carbon, circularity and material-reuse indicators, building monitoring, sensor data, Post-Occupancy Evaluation (PoE), and feedback from building operation into future design decisions.

The methods will be developed and tested through the REGEN4BE Fribourg demonstration activities, using Smart Living Lab data and infrastructure in close collaboration with the Building2050 team.

As an integrated strand of the doctoral thesis, the candidate will apply and adapt the REGEN4BE framework to selected earth-block and Limestone Calcined Clay Cement (LC3)-based housing systems in African contexts. Building on SONO’s projects and partnerships, this research will examine how local materials, passive environmental strategies, construction processes, whole-life carbon, circularity, repairability, measured building performance and residents’ experience can inform regenerative design.

The European and African research strands will form one coherent doctoral project. The candidate will contribute to a generic interoperability framework within REGEN4BE and assess its transferability and necessary adaptation across different materials, climates, construction cultures and levels of digital infrastructure.

Main duties and responsibilities

As a PhD Student, you will take scientific responsibility for developing and completing your doctoral dissertation, formulate original research questions, and establish a rigorous methodology. You will conduct computational, experimental and field-based research in collaboration with academic, technical, institutional, software-development and industry partners. Your responsibilities will include collecting, managing, analysing and interpreting quantitative and qualitative data, preparing articles for peer-reviewed journals, presenting findings at conferences, workshops and project meetings, contributing to REGEN4BE deliverables, demonstrations and dissemination activities, and participating in teaching and, where appropriate, the supervision of student projects.

Within REGEN4BE, you will contribute to the development and scientific validation of the Regenerative Design Intelligence Platform (REDIP) and its building-data and performance-assessment workflows. You will develop and test interoperable methods linking BIM, openBIM and IFC with building-energy models, Life-Cycle Assessment, whole-life-carbon calculations, circularity indicators, monitoring data, occupant feedback and Post-Occupancy Evaluation. You will investigate data continuity, traceability, uncertainty and interoperability across the design, construction and operational phases of buildings, and define information requirements and data structures for exchanging geometry, materials, environmental indicators, measured performance and occupant feedback across digital environments.

You will establish protocols for assessing the reliability, accuracy, completeness, reproducibility and usability of the proposed workflows. Using Smart Living Lab datasets and infrastructure, you will undertake full-scale testing, data collection, model calibration and scientific validation in Fribourg. You will compare predicted and simulated performance with measured environmental conditions and occupant experience, and collaborate with Building2050, relevant EPFL laboratories and ENAC research platforms, including PL-MTI where applicable. You will also support the scientific specification, testing and validation of APIs, connectors, data pipelines and interfaces in coordination with the project’s software-development partners, and assess the transferability of the methods across REGEN4BE demonstration sites and different building, climatic and institutional contexts.

As part of the doctoral thesis, you will apply and adapt the REGEN4BE framework to selected SONO housing projects and partnerships in Africa. You will develop BIM information structures for earth blocks, compressed and stabilised-earth systems, LC3-based blocks, mortars, concrete components and related assemblies, incorporating locally specific material and construction data. You will investigate BIM-to-BEM workflows for passive environmental performance, including thermal mass, solar protection, natural ventilation, indoor air movement, temperature, humidity and occupant-controlled openings. You will also develop BIM-linked LCA, whole-life-carbon and circularity methods for locally produced, low-carbon and repairable construction, determine which methods are transferable and which require adaptation to local climatic, material, economic, technical and social conditions, and translate the findings into design recommendations and decision-support methods for climate-responsive and regenerative housing.

Profile

• A Master’s degree in architecture, architectural engineering, building science, civil engineering, mechanical engineering, computational design, environmental engineering, or a related field

• Strong interest in the intersection of architectural design, building technology, environmental performance, and digital methods

• Experience with BIM workflows and an interest in open, interoperable digital environments, including IFC

• Knowledge or experience in one or more of the following areas:
- building energy modelling and simulation;
- Life Cycle Assessment;
- embodied- and operational-carbon assessment;
- circular construction;
- building monitoring and Post-Occupancy Evaluation;
- computational design;
- building-data interoperability

• Strong data-analysis skills and the ability to work with heterogeneous datasets from digital models, simulations, environmental databases, sensors, surveys, and interviews

• Experience in scientific programming, scripting, or workflow automation. Knowledge of Python or an equivalent language is highly desirable

• Experience with APIs, databases, visual programming, parametric design, or data visualization is an asset.
Interest in earth construction, low-carbon cementitious systems, LC3, passive environmental design, and housing in African contexts

• Interest in full-scale experimentation, Living Labs, and the links between research, design, construction, building operation, and occupant experience

• Ability to conduct fieldwork and collaborate with researchers, professionals, contractors, institutions, communities, and residents

• Capacity to formulate original research questions, develop rigorous validation methods, and communicate findings through peer-reviewed scientific publications

• Excellent written and spoken English; French is an asset

• Scientific autonomy, intellectual curiosity, and the ability to work effectively in an interdisciplinary and international research environment.

We offer

• Four years to complete your PhD, with competitive remuneration according to EPFL employment conditions

• Membership in the EPFL Doctoral Program in Architecture and Sciences of the City—EDAR, subject to formal admission by the programme

• An opportunity to develop a distinctive scientific profile at the intersection of regenerative design, building-data interoperability, environmental simulation, whole-life-carbon assessment, circular construction, building monitoring and low-carbon materials

• Participation in a major international Horizon Europe consortium involving academic, public, technical, design and industry partners

• A world-class research and training environment with access to the Smart Living Lab, Building2050 expertise and relevant EPFL research infrastructure

• Opportunities for full-scale experimentation, international collaboration and field research connected to SONO’s projects and partnerships

• A multicultural and stimulating working environment at EPFL’s Fribourg associated campus

• A one-year fixed-term contract, renewable annually for a total planned duration of four years, subject to satisfactory progress and applicable EPFL employment conditions.

Informations

The doctoral candidate will be based at the South–North Laboratory for Sustainable Construction and Conservation—SONO Lab, within EPFL’s School of Architecture, Civil and Environmental Engineering, at the EPFL Fribourg associated campus. The thesis will be supervised by Prof. Aziza Chaouni.

The candidate will collaborate closely with, the REGEN4BE consortium; Smart Living Lab researchers and technical teams; Building2050; relevant EPFL laboratories and research platforms; SONO Lab’s academic and institutional partners in Africa; local researchers, professionals, construction partners, communities and building users involved in the selected case studies.

Application documents

Applications must include:

• A one-page motivation letter explaining your interest in the position and how your experience relates to the proposed research

• A detailed curriculum vitae, including your address, email and telephone number

• Copies of university diplomas and academic transcripts

• A research statement of no more than two pages outlining your relevant methodological experience and initial research interests

• One representative sample of relevant work, such as a publication, portfolio, thesis excerpt, research report, computational portfolio or technical project

• The names, affiliations and contact details of three referees willing to provide recommendations.

Please do not upload reference letters with the recruitment application. Only the referees’ names and contact details are required at this stage. They may later be contacted directly by the hiring manager. The separate EDAR application follows its own confidential recommendation procedure.

PhD application deadline: 1st October 2026
EDAR application deadline: 15 September 2026
Contract start date: 15 January 2027
Activity rate: 100%
Contract type: Fixed-term contract—CDD
Duration: Four years, from 15 January 2027 to 14 January 2031

For questions regarding the scientific content of the position, please contact aziza.chaouni@epfl.ch.

Applications must be submitted through the official EPFL recruitment platform. Applications sent by email will not be considered formal applications

descriptionByLocale.it:
Missione

Il South-North Laboratory for Sustainable Construction and Conservation (SONO Lab) di EPFL sta reclutando un PhD Student a tempo pieno (100%) all'interno della School of Architecture, Civil and Environmental Engineering (ENAC), con sede presso il campus associato di EPFL Fribourg.

SONO Lab indaga gli approcci a basso tenore di carbonio, a risposta climatica e socialmente inclusi per la progettazione, la costruzione e la conservazione. La sua ricerca combina il design architettonico, la valutazione ambientale, i metodi digitali, la sperimentazione su larga scala, il monitoraggio delle prestazioni edilizie e gli approcci partecipativi, con particolare attenzione alle collaborazioni tra Europa e Africa.

Il candidato di successo contribuirà a REGEN4BE — Design rigenerativo per l'ambiente costruito, un progetto Horizon Europe sviluppato nell'ambito del nuovo quadro europeo Bauhaus. REGEN4BE cerca di rendere il design rigenerativo misurabile, interoperabile e scalabile attraverso strumenti digitali, materiali innovativi, processi partecipativi, Living Labs e sviluppo delle politiche. I suoi risultati includono un quadro di valutazione rigenerativa e la piattaforma di intelligence per il design rigenerativo (REDIP). Fribourg è uno dei siti europei di dimostrazione e replica del progetto.

All'interno di REGEN4BE, il candidato svilupperà e convalidarà scientificamente i flussi di lavoro digitali interoperabili che collegano Building Information Modelling (BIM), Building Energy Modelling (BEM), Life-Cycle Assessment (LCA), carbonio incorporato e operativo, indicatori di circolarità e di riutilizzo dei materiali, monitoraggio degli edifici, dati dei sensori, valutazione post-Occupancy (PoE), e feedback dall'operazione di costruzione alle future decisioni di progettazione.

I metodi saranno sviluppati e testati attraverso le attività dimostrative REGEN4BE Fribourg, utilizzando i dati e le infrastrutture Smart Living Lab in stretta collaborazione con il team Building2050.

Come filo integrato della tesi di dottorato, il candidato applicherà e adattarà il quadro REGEN4BE a blocchi terrestri selezionati e Limestone Calcined Clay Cement (LC3)-based sistemi di alloggio in contesti africani. Sulla base dei progetti e dei partenariati di SONO, questa ricerca esaminerà come materiali locali, strategie ambientali passive, processi costruttivi, carbonio di vita intera, circolarità, riparabilità, prestazioni di costruzione misurate e l’esperienza dei residenti possano informare il design rigenerativo.

I settori della ricerca europea e africana costituiranno un progetto medico coerente. Il candidato contribuirà ad un generico quadro di interoperabilità all'interno di REGEN4BE e valuterà la sua trasferibilità e l'adattamento necessario in diversi materiali, climi, culture edili e livelli di infrastruttura digitale.

Principali doveri e responsabilità

Come studente di dottorato, si assumerà la responsabilità scientifica per lo sviluppo e il completamento della vostra tesi di dottorato, formulare domande di ricerca originali, e stabilire una metodologia rigorosa. Condurrai ricerche computazionali, sperimentali e basate sul campo in collaborazione con partner accademici, tecnici, istituzionali, software-sviluppo e industria. Le tue responsabilità includono la raccolta, la gestione, l'analisi e l'interpretazione di dati quantitativi e qualitativi, la preparazione di articoli per riviste peer-reviewed, la presentazione dei risultati a conferenze, workshop e incontri di progetto, contribuendo a REGEN4BE consegnabili, dimostrazioni e attività di diffusione, e la partecipazione all'insegnamento e, se del caso, alla supervisione dei progetti studenteschi.

All'interno di REGEN4BE, contribuirai allo sviluppo e alla validazione scientifica della Piattaforma di Intelligenza del Design Rigenerativo (REDIP) e dei suoi flussi di lavoro di data ed esecuzione-valutazione. Svilupperai e testerai metodi interoperabili che collegano BIM, OpenBIM e IFC con modelli di costruzione-energia, valutazione del ciclo di vita, calcoli interi-vita-carbonio, indicatori di circolarità, dati di monitoraggio, feedback degli occupanti e valutazione post-Occupancy. Indagherete la continuità dei dati, la tracciabilità, l'incertezza e l'interoperabilità attraverso la progettazione, la costruzione e le fasi operative degli edifici, e definire i requisiti di informazione e le strutture dei dati per lo scambio di geometria, materiali, indicatori ambientali, prestazioni misurate e feedback degli occupanti in ambienti digitali.

Stabilirai protocolli per valutare l'affidabilità, l'accuratezza, la completezza, la riproducibilità e l'usabilità dei flussi di lavoro proposti. Utilizzando i dataset e le infrastrutture di Smart Living Lab, effettuerai test su larga scala, raccolta dati, calibrazione dei modelli e validazione scientifica a Fribourg. Potrai confrontare le prestazioni prevedibili e simulate con le condizioni ambientali misurate e l'esperienza occupante, e collaborare con Building2050, laboratori EPFL pertinenti e piattaforme di ricerca ENAC, tra cui PL-MTI, dove applicabile. Sosterrai anche le specifiche scientifiche, i test e la validazione di API, connettori, datadotti e interfacce in coordinamento con i partner di sviluppo software del progetto, e valuterai la trasferibilità dei metodi attraverso i siti dimostrativi REGEN4BE e diversi contesti costruttivi, climatici e istituzionali.

Nell'ambito della tesi di dottorato, si applica e si adatta il quadro REGEN4BE a progetti e partenariati SONO selezionati in Africa. Svilupperai strutture informative BIM per blocchi di terra, sistemi di terra compressi e stabilizzati, blocchi basati su LC3, mortai, componenti in calcestruzzo e assemblaggi correlati, incorporando materiali e dati di costruzione localmente specifici. Indagherete i flussi di lavoro BIM-to-BEM per le prestazioni ambientali passive, tra cui massa termica, protezione solare, ventilazione naturale, movimento dell'aria interna, temperatura, umidità e aperture controllate dagli occupanti. Svilupperai anche i metodi LCA, full-life-carbon e circolari per la costruzione localmente prodotta, a basso tenore di carbonio e riparabile, determinano quali metodi sono trasferibili e che richiedono l'adattamento alle condizioni climatiche, materiali, economiche, tecniche e sociali locali, e traducono i risultati in raccomandazioni di progettazione e metodi di supporto decisionale per l'alloggio responsabile e rigenerativo del clima.

Profilo

• Laurea Magistrale in architettura, ingegneria architettonica, scienze della costruzione, ingegneria civile, ingegneria meccanica, progettazione computazionale, ingegneria ambientale, o un campo correlato

• Forte interesse per l'intersezione di progettazione architettonica, tecnologia di costruzione, prestazioni ambientali e metodi digitali

• Esperienza con flussi di lavoro BIM e interesse per ambienti digitali aperti e interoperabili, tra cui IFC

• Conoscenza o esperienza in una o più delle seguenti aree:
- costruzione di modelli di energia e simulazione;
- Valutazione del ciclo di vita;
- valutazione corporea e operativa-carbonio;
- costruzione circolare;
- monitoraggio della costruzione e valutazione post-operatoria;
- progettazione computazionale;
- interoperabilità dei dati

• Forte capacità di analisi dei dati e la capacità di lavorare con dataset eterogenei da modelli digitali, simulazioni, database ambientali, sensori, sondaggi e interviste

• Esperienza nella programmazione scientifica, scrittura o automazione del flusso di lavoro. La conoscenza di Python o di un linguaggio equivalente è altamente auspicabile

• Esperienza con API, database, programmazione visiva, progettazione parametrica o visualizzazione dei dati è un bene.
Interessi nella costruzione della terra, sistemi cementizi a basso tenore di carbonio, LC3, progettazione ambientale passiva e alloggiamento in contesti africani

• Interessi nella sperimentazione su larga scala, Living Labs, e i collegamenti tra ricerca, progettazione, costruzione, operazione di costruzione e esperienza occupante

• Capacità di condurre il lavoro sul campo e collaborare con ricercatori, professionisti, appaltatori, istituzioni, comunità e residenti

• Capacità di formulare domande di ricerca originali, sviluppare metodi di validazione rigorosi e comunicare i risultati attraverso pubblicazioni scientifiche peer-reviewed

• Ottimo scritto e parlato inglese; il francese è un bene

• L'autonomia scientifica, la curiosità intellettuale e la capacità di lavorare efficacemente in un ambiente di ricerca interdisciplinare e internazionale.

Offriamo

• Quattro anni per completare il dottorato, con una remunerazione competitiva secondo le condizioni di occupazione EPFL

• Membership in EPFL Dottoral Program in Architettura e Scienze della Città—EDAR, previa ammissione formale da parte del programma

• Un'opportunità per sviluppare un profilo scientifico distintivo all'intersezione del design rigenerativo, dell'interoperabilità dei dati di costruzione, della simulazione ambientale, della valutazione dell'intero-vita-carbonio, della costruzione circolare, del monitoraggio degli edifici e dei materiali a basso tenore di carbonio

• Partecipazione a un importante consorzio internazionale Horizon Europe che coinvolge partner accademici, pubblici, tecnici, design e industriali

• Un ambiente di ricerca e formazione di livello mondiale con accesso allo Smart Living Lab, alle competenze di Building2050 e alle pertinenti infrastrutture di ricerca EPFL

• Opportunità di sperimentazione su larga scala, collaborazione internazionale e ricerca sul campo connesse ai progetti e alle partnership di SONO

• Un ambiente di lavoro multiculturale e stimolante presso il campus associato di Fribourg di EPFL

• Un contratto a tempo determinato di un anno, rinnovabile annualmente per una durata totale prevista di quattro anni, soggetto a progressi soddisfacenti e condizioni di occupazione EPFL applicabili.

Informazioni

Il candidato medico si baserà presso il South-North Laboratory for Sustainable Construction and Conservation—SONO Lab, all'interno della Scuola di Architettura dell'EPFL, Ingegneria Civile e Ambientale, presso il campus associato di EPFL Fribourg. La tesi sarà supervisionata dal Prof. Aziza Chaouni.

Il candidato collaborerà a stretto contatto con il consorzio REGEN4BE; ricercatori e team tecnici di Smart Living Lab; Building2050; laboratori EPFL rilevanti e piattaforme di ricerca; partner accademici e istituzionali di SONO Lab in Africa; ricercatori locali, professionisti, partner di costruzione, comunità e utenti di costruzione coinvolti negli studi di casi selezionati.

Documenti di domanda

Le domande devono includere:

• Una lettera di motivazione di una pagina che spiega il vostro interesse nella posizione e come la vostra esperienza si riferisce alla ricerca proposta

• Un curriculum vitae dettagliato, compreso il tuo indirizzo, email e numero di telefono

• Copie di diplomi universitari e trascrizioni accademiche

• Una dichiarazione di ricerca non più di due pagine che illustra la vostra esperienza metodologica rilevante e gli interessi iniziali della ricerca

• Un campione rappresentativo di lavori rilevanti, come una pubblicazione, un portafoglio, un estratto di tesi, un rapporto di ricerca, un portafoglio computazionale o un progetto tecnico

descriptionByLocale.en:
Mission

The South–North Laboratory for Sustainable Construction and Conservation (SONO Lab) at EPFL is recruiting a full-time PhD Student (100%) within the School of Architecture, Civil and Environmental Engineering (ENAC), based at the EPFL Fribourg associated campus.

SONO Lab investigates low-carbon, climate-responsive and socially inclusive approaches to building design, construction and conservation. Its research combines architectural design, environmental assessment, digital methods, full-scale experimentation, building-performance monitoring and participatory approaches, with a particular focus on collaborations between Europe and Africa.

The successful candidate will contribute to REGEN4BE—Regenerative Design for the Built Environment, a Horizon Europe project developed within the New European Bauhaus framework. REGEN4BE seeks to make regenerative design measurable, interoperable and scalable through digital tools, innovative materials, participatory processes, Living Labs and policy development. Its outputs include a Regenerative Evaluation Framework and the Regenerative Design Intelligence Platform (REDIP). Fribourg is one of the project’s European demonstration and replication sites.

Within REGEN4BE, the candidate will develop and scientifically validate interoperable digital workflows linking Building Information Modelling (BIM), Building Energy Modelling (BEM), Life-Cycle Assessment (LCA), embodied and operational carbon, circularity and material-reuse indicators, building monitoring, sensor data, Post-Occupancy Evaluation (PoE), and feedback from building operation into future design decisions.

The methods will be developed and tested through the REGEN4BE Fribourg demonstration activities, using Smart Living Lab data and infrastructure in close collaboration with the Building2050 team.

As an integrated strand of the doctoral thesis, the candidate will apply and adapt the REGEN4BE framework to selected earth-block and Limestone Calcined Clay Cement (LC3)-based housing systems in African contexts. Building on SONO’s projects and partnerships, this research will examine how local materials, passive environmental strategies, construction processes, whole-life carbon, circularity, repairability, measured building performance and residents’ experience can inform regenerative design.

The European and African research strands will form one coherent doctoral project. The candidate will contribute to a generic interoperability framework within REGEN4BE and assess its transferability and necessary adaptation across different materials, climates, construction cultures and levels of digital infrastructure.

Main duties and responsibilities

As a PhD Student, you will take scientific responsibility for developing and completing your doctoral dissertation, formulate original research questions, and establish a rigorous methodology. You will conduct computational, experimental and field-based research in collaboration with academic, technical, institutional, software-development and industry partners. Your responsibilities will include collecting, managing, analysing and interpreting quantitative and qualitative data, preparing articles for peer-reviewed journals, presenting findings at conferences, workshops and project meetings, contributing to REGEN4BE deliverables, demonstrations and dissemination activities, and participating in teaching and, where appropriate, the supervision of student projects.

Within REGEN4BE, you will contribute to the development and scientific validation of the Regenerative Design Intelligence Platform (REDIP) and its building-data and performance-assessment workflows. You will develop and test interoperable methods linking BIM, openBIM and IFC with building-energy models, Life-Cycle Assessment, whole-life-carbon calculations, circularity indicators, monitoring data, occupant feedback and Post-Occupancy Evaluation. You will investigate data continuity, traceability, uncertainty and interoperability across the design, construction and operational phases of buildings, and define information requirements and data structures for exchanging geometry, materials, environmental indicators, measured performance and occupant feedback across digital environments.

You will establish protocols for assessing the reliability, accuracy, completeness, reproducibility and usability of the proposed workflows. Using Smart Living Lab datasets and infrastructure, you will undertake full-scale testing, data collection, model calibration and scientific validation in Fribourg. You will compare predicted and simulated performance with measured environmental conditions and occupant experience, and collaborate with Building2050, relevant EPFL laboratories and ENAC research platforms, including PL-MTI where applicable. You will also support the scientific specification, testing and validation of APIs, connectors, data pipelines and interfaces in coordination with the project’s software-development partners, and assess the transferability of the methods across REGEN4BE demonstration sites and different building, climatic and institutional contexts.

As part of the doctoral thesis, you will apply and adapt the REGEN4BE framework to selected SONO housing projects and partnerships in Africa. You will develop BIM information structures for earth blocks, compressed and stabilised-earth systems, LC3-based blocks, mortars, concrete components and related assemblies, incorporating locally specific material and construction data. You will investigate BIM-to-BEM workflows for passive environmental performance, including thermal mass, solar protection, natural ventilation, indoor air movement, temperature, humidity and occupant-controlled openings. You will also develop BIM-linked LCA, whole-life-carbon and circularity methods for locally produced, low-carbon and repairable construction, determine which methods are transferable and which require adaptation to local climatic, material, economic, technical and social conditions, and translate the findings into design recommendations and decision-support methods for climate-responsive and regenerative housing.

Profile

• A Master’s degree in architecture, architectural engineering, building science, civil engineering, mechanical engineering, computational design, environmental engineering, or a related field

• Strong interest in the intersection of architectural design, building technology, environmental performance, and digital methods

• Experience with BIM workflows and an interest in open, interoperable digital environments, including IFC

• Knowledge or experience in one or more of the following areas:
- building energy modelling and simulation;
- Life Cycle Assessment;
- embodied- and operational-carbon assessment;
- circular construction;
- building monitoring and Post-Occupancy Evaluation;
- computational design;
- building-data interoperability

• Strong data-analysis skills and the ability to work with heterogeneous datasets from digital models, simulations, environmental databases, sensors, surveys, and interviews

• Experience in scientific programming, scripting, or workflow automation. Knowledge of Python or an equivalent language is highly desirable

• Experience with APIs, databases, visual programming, parametric design, or data visualization is an asset.
Interest in earth construction, low-carbon cementitious systems, LC3, passive environmental design, and housing in African contexts

• Interest in full-scale experimentation, Living Labs, and the links between research, design, construction, building operation, and occupant experience

• Ability to conduct fieldwork and collaborate with researchers, professionals, contractors, institutions, communities, and residents

• Capacity to formulate original research questions, develop rigorous validation methods, and communicate findings through peer-reviewed scientific publications

• Excellent written and spoken English; French is an asset

• Scientific autonomy, intellectual curiosity, and the ability to work effectively in an interdisciplinary and international research environment.

We offer

• Four years to complete your PhD, with competitive remuneration according to EPFL employment conditions

• Membership in the EPFL Doctoral Program in Architecture and Sciences of the City—EDAR, subject to formal admission by the programme

• An opportunity to develop a distinctive scientific profile at the intersection of regenerative design, building-data interoperability, environmental simulation, whole-life-carbon assessment, circular construction, building monitoring and low-carbon materials

• Participation in a major international Horizon Europe consortium involving academic, public, technical, design and industry partners

• A world-class research and training environment with access to the Smart Living Lab, Building2050 expertise and relevant EPFL research infrastructure

• Opportunities for full-scale experimentation, international collaboration and field research connected to SONO’s projects and partnerships

• A multicultural and stimulating working environment at EPFL’s Fribourg associated campus

• A one-year fixed-term contract, renewable annually for a total planned duration of four years, subject to satisfactory progress and applicable EPFL employment conditions.

Informations

The doctoral candidate will be based at the South–North Laboratory for Sustainable Construction and Conservation—SONO Lab, within EPFL’s School of Architecture, Civil and Environmental Engineering, at the EPFL Fribourg associated campus. The thesis will be supervised by Prof. Aziza Chaouni.

The candidate will collaborate closely with, the REGEN4BE consortium; Smart Living Lab researchers and technical teams; Building2050; relevant EPFL laboratories and research platforms; SONO Lab’s academic and institutional partners in Africa; local researchers, professionals, construction partners, communities and building users involved in the selected case studies.

Application documents

Applications must include:

• A one-page motivation letter explaining your interest in the position and how your experience relates to the proposed research

• A detailed curriculum vitae, including your address, email and telephone number

• Copies of university diplomas and academic transcripts

• A research statement of no more than two pages outlining your relevant methodological experience and initial research interests

• One representative sample of relevant work, such as a publication, portfolio, thesis excerpt, research report, computational portfolio or technical project

• The names, affiliations and contact details of three referees willing to provide recommendations.

Please do not upload reference letters with the recruitment application. Only the referees’ names and contact details are required at this stage. They may later be contacted directly by the hiring manager. The separate EDAR application follows its own confidential recommendation procedure.

For questions regarding the scientific content of the position, please contact aziza.chaouni@epfl.ch.

descriptionByLocale.de:
Mission

Das Süd-Nord-Labor für nachhaltiges Bauen und Konservieren (SONO Lab) an der EPFL rekrutiert einen Vollzeit-Doktoranden (100%) innerhalb der School of Architecture, Civil and Environmental Engineering (ENAC) mit Sitz auf dem EPFL Fribourg assoziierten Campus.

SONO Lab untersucht kohlenstoffarme, klimaresponsive und sozial integrative Ansätze für Gebäudeplanung, Bau und Erhaltung. Seine Forschung kombiniert architektonische Gestaltung, Umweltverträglichkeitsprüfung, digitale Methoden, umfassende Experimente, Überwachung der Gebäudeleistung und partizipative Ansätze mit einem besonderen Fokus auf die Zusammenarbeit zwischen Europa und Afrika.

Der erfolgreiche Kandidat wird einen Beitrag zu REGEN4BE – Regenerative Design for the Built Environment leisten, einem Horizon Europe-Projekt, das im Rahmen des Neuen Europäischen Bauhauses entwickelt wurde. REGEN4BE will regeneratives Design durch digitale Tools, innovative Materialien, partizipative Prozesse, Living Labs und Politikentwicklung messbar, interoperabel und skalierbar machen. Zu den Ergebnissen gehören ein Regenerative Evaluation Framework und die Regenerative Design Intelligence Platform (REDIP). Fribourg ist einer der europäischen Demonstrations- und Replikationsstandorte des Projekts.

Innerhalb von REGEN4BE wird der Kandidat interoperable digitale Workflows entwickeln und wissenschaftlich validieren, die Building Information Modeling (BIM), Building Energy Modeling (BEM), Life-Cycle Assessment (LCA), verkörperte und operative Kohlenstoff-, Zirkularitäts- und Materialwiederverwendungsindikatoren, Gebäudeüberwachung, Sensordaten, Post-Occupancy Evaluation (PoE) und Feedback aus dem Gebäudebetrieb zu zukünftigen Designentscheidungen verbinden.

Die Methoden werden im Rahmen der REGEN4BE-Demonstrationsaktivitäten in Fribourg entwickelt und getestet, wobei Daten und Infrastruktur des Smart Living Lab in enger Zusammenarbeit mit dem Team von Building2050 verwendet werden.

Als integrierter Teil der Doktorarbeit wird der Kandidat das REGEN4BE-Framework auf ausgewählte Erdblock- und Kalkstein-Tonzement (LC3)-basierte Gehäusesysteme im afrikanischen Kontext anwenden und anpassen. Aufbauend auf den Projekten und Partnerschaften von SONO wird diese Forschung untersuchen, wie lokale Materialien, passive Umweltstrategien, Bauprozesse, Kohlenstoff aus der gesamten Lebensdauer, Zirkularität, Reparaturfähigkeit, gemessene Gebäudeleistung und die Erfahrung der Bewohner das regenerative Design beeinflussen können.

Die europäischen und afrikanischen Forschungsstränge werden ein zusammenhängendes Doktorandenprojekt bilden. Der Kandidat wird zu einem generischen Interoperabilitätsrahmen innerhalb von REGEN4BE beitragen und seine Übertragbarkeit und notwendige Anpassung an verschiedene Materialien, Klimazonen, Baukulturen und Ebenen der digitalen Infrastruktur bewerten.

Hauptaufgaben und Zuständigkeiten

Als Doktorand übernehmen Sie die wissenschaftliche Verantwortung für die Entwicklung und den Abschluss Ihrer Dissertation, formulieren originelle Forschungsfragen und etablieren eine strenge Methodik. Sie werden computergestützte, experimentelle und feldbasierte Forschung in Zusammenarbeit mit akademischen, technischen, institutionellen, Softwareentwicklungs- und Industriepartnern durchführen. Ihre Aufgaben umfassen das Sammeln, Verwalten, Analysieren und Interpretieren quantitativer und qualitativer Daten, die Vorbereitung von Artikeln für von Experten begutachtete Zeitschriften, die Präsentation von Ergebnissen auf Konferenzen, Workshops und Projekttreffen, den Beitrag zu REGEN4BE-Ergebnissen, Demonstrationen und Verbreitungsaktivitäten sowie die Teilnahme an der Lehre und gegebenenfalls der Überwachung von Studentenprojekten.

Innerhalb von REGEN4BE tragen Sie zur Entwicklung und wissenschaftlichen Validierung der Regenerative Design Intelligence Platform (REDIP) und ihrer Workflows für Gebäudedaten und Leistungsbewertung bei. Sie entwickeln und testen interoperable Methoden, die BIM, openBIM und IFC mit Gebäudeenergiemodellen, Life-Cycle-Bewertung, Gesamtlebenskohlenstoffberechnungen, Zirkularitätsindikatoren, Überwachungsdaten, Insassen-Feedback und Post-Occupancy-Bewertung verbinden. Sie untersuchen Datenkontinuität, Rückverfolgbarkeit, Unsicherheit und Interoperabilität in den Planungs-, Bau- und Betriebsphasen von Gebäuden und definieren Informationsanforderungen und Datenstrukturen für den Austausch von Geometrie, Materialien, Umweltindikatoren, gemessener Leistung und Benutzerrückmeldung in digitalen Umgebungen.

Sie erstellen Protokolle zur Beurteilung der Zuverlässigkeit, Genauigkeit, Vollständigkeit, Reproduzierbarkeit und Nutzbarkeit der vorgeschlagenen Workflows. Mit Smart Living Lab-Datensätzen und Infrastruktur werden Sie in Freiburg Tests, Datenerfassung, Modellkalibrierung und wissenschaftliche Validierung durchführen. Sie vergleichen die vorhergesagte und simulierte Leistung mit den gemessenen Umweltbedingungen und der Erfahrung der Bewohner und arbeiten mit Building2050, den relevanten EPFL-Labors und ENAC-Forschungsplattformen, einschließlich PL-MTI, zusammen. Sie unterstützen auch die wissenschaftliche Spezifikation, Prüfung und Validierung von APIs, Konnektoren, Datenpipelines und Schnittstellen in Abstimmung mit den Softwareentwicklungspartnern des Projekts und bewerten die Übertragbarkeit der Methoden über REGEN4BE-Demonstrationsstandorte und verschiedene Gebäude-, Klima- und institutionelle Kontexte hinweg.

Im Rahmen der Doktorarbeit werden Sie das REGEN4BE Framework auf ausgewählte SONO Wohnprojekte und Partnerschaften in Afrika anwenden und anpassen. Sie entwickeln BIM-Informationsstrukturen für Erdblöcke, komprimierte und stabilisierte Erdsysteme, LC3-basierte Blöcke, Mörtel, Betonkomponenten und verwandte Baugruppen unter Einbeziehung lokal spezifischer Material- und Baudaten. Sie werden BIM-to-BEM-Workflows auf passive Umweltleistung untersuchen, einschließlich thermischer Masse, Sonnenschutz, natürlicher Lüftung, Luftbewegung in Innenräumen, Temperatur, Feuchtigkeit und von den Bewohnern kontrollierte Öffnungen. Sie werden auch BIM-verknüpfte LCA-, Whole-Life-Carbon- und Circularity-Methoden für lokal produziertes, kohlenstoffarmes und reparierbares Bauen entwickeln, bestimmen, welche Methoden übertragbar sind und welche eine Anpassung an lokale klimatische, materielle, wirtschaftliche, technische und soziale Bedingungen erfordern, und die Ergebnisse in Designempfehlungen und Entscheidungshilfemethoden für klimaresponsives und regeneratives Wohnen umsetzen.

Profil

• Ein Master-Abschluss in Architektur, Architekturingenieurwesen, Bauwissenschaften, Bauingenieurwesen, Maschinenbau, Computerdesign, Umwelttechnik oder einem verwandten Bereich

• Starkes Interesse an der Schnittstelle von Architektur, Gebäudetechnik, Umweltleistung und digitalen Methoden

• Erfahrung mit BIM-Workflows und Interesse an offenen, interoperablen digitalen Umgebungen, einschließlich IFC

• Kenntnisse oder Erfahrungen in einem oder mehreren der folgenden Bereiche:
- Modellierung und Simulation von Gebäudeenergie;
- Bewertung des Lebenszyklus;
- Bewertung der verkörperten und der betrieblichen CO2-Emissionen;
- kreisförmige Bauweise;
- Gebäudeüberwachung und Bewertung nach Belegung;
- Computerdesign;
- Interoperabilität von Gebäudedaten

• Starke Datenanalysefähigkeiten und die Fähigkeit, mit heterogenen Datensätzen aus digitalen Modellen, Simulationen, Umweltdatenbanken, Sensoren, Umfragen und Interviews zu arbeiten

• Erfahrung in der wissenschaftlichen Programmierung, Scripting oder Workflow-Automatisierung. Kenntnisse in Python oder einer gleichwertigen Sprache sind sehr wünschenswert

• Erfahrung mit APIs, Datenbanken, visueller Programmierung, parametrischem Design oder Datenvisualisierung ist eine Bereicherung.
Interesse an Erdbau, kohlenstoffarmen Zementsystemen, LC3, passivem Umweltdesign und Wohnen im afrikanischen Kontext

• Interesse an umfassenden Experimenten, Living Labs und den Verbindungen zwischen Forschung, Design, Bau, Baubetrieb und Benutzererfahrung

• Fähigkeit, Feldforschung durchzuführen und mit Forschern, Fachleuten, Auftragnehmern, Institutionen, Gemeinschaften und Bewohnern zusammenzuarbeiten

• Fähigkeit, originelle Forschungsfragen zu formulieren, strenge Validierungsmethoden zu entwickeln und Ergebnisse durch peer-reviewte wissenschaftliche Publikationen zu kommunizieren

• Ausgezeichnetes geschriebenes und gesprochenes Englisch; Französisch ist ein Asset

• Wissenschaftliche Autonomie, intellektuelle Neugier und die Fähigkeit, in einem interdisziplinären und internationalen Forschungsumfeld effektiv zu arbeiten.

Wir bieten

• Vier Jahre, um Ihre Promotion abzuschließen, mit wettbewerbsfähiger Vergütung gemäß den Beschäftigungsbedingungen der EPFL

• Mitgliedschaft im EPFL-Doktorandenprogramm für Architektur und Wissenschaften der Stadt - EDAR, vorbehaltlich der formellen Zulassung durch das Programm

• Eine Gelegenheit, ein unverwechselbares wissenschaftliches Profil an der Schnittstelle von regenerativem Design, Gebäudedaten-Interoperabilität, Umweltsimulation, Gesamtkohlenstoffbewertung, Kreislaufkonstruktion, Gebäudeüberwachung und kohlenstoffarmen Materialien zu entwickeln

• Teilnahme an einem großen internationalen Horizon Europe-Konsortium mit akademischen, öffentlichen, technischen, Design- und Industriepartnern

• Eine Weltklasse-Forschungs- und Ausbildungsumgebung mit Zugang zum Smart Living Lab, dem Building2050-Know-how und der relevanten EPFL-Forschungsinfrastruktur

• Ein einjähriger befristeter Vertrag, der jährlich für eine geplante Gesamtlaufzeit von vier Jahren verlängert werden kann, vorbehaltlich zufriedenstellender Fortschritte und geltender Beschäftigungsbedingungen der EPFL.

Informationen

Antragsunterlagen

Mission

Le Laboratoire Sud-Nord pour la Construction et la Conservation Durables (SONO Lab) de l'EPFL recrute un doctorant à temps plein (100%) au sein de l'Ecole d'Architecture, Génie Civil et Environnemental (ENAC), basée sur le campus associé à l'EPFL Fribourg.

SONO Lab étudie les approches à faible émission de carbone, adaptées au climat et socialement inclusives de la conception, de la construction et de la conservation des bâtiments. Sa recherche combine la conception architecturale, l'évaluation environnementale, les méthodes numériques, l'expérimentation à grande échelle, le suivi des performances du bâtiment et les approches participatives, en mettant l'accent sur les collaborations entre l'Europe et l'Afrique.

Le candidat retenu participera au projet REGEN4BE – Design régénératif pour l'environnement bâti, un projet Horizon Europe développé dans le cadre du nouveau Bauhaus européen. REGEN4BE cherche à rendre la conception régénératrice mesurable, interopérable et évolutive grâce à des outils numériques, des matériaux innovants, des processus participatifs, des laboratoires vivants et l'élaboration de politiques. Ses résultats comprennent un cadre d'évaluation régénératrice et la plateforme d'intelligence de conception régénératrice (REDIP). Fribourg est l'un des sites européens de démonstration et de réplication du projet.

Au sein de REGEN4BE, le candidat élaborera et validera scientifiquement des flux de travail numériques interopérables reliant la modélisation de l'information sur les bâtiments (BIM), la modélisation de l'énergie des bâtiments (BEM), l'évaluation du cycle de vie (LCA), des indicateurs de carbone, de la circularité et de la réutilisation des matériaux, la surveillance des bâtiments, les données des capteurs, l'évaluation post-occupation (EP) et la rétroaction de l'exploitation des bâtiments aux futures décisions de conception.

Les méthodes seront développées et testées dans le cadre des activités de démonstration REGEN4BE Fribourg, en utilisant les données et l'infrastructure du Smart Living Lab en étroite collaboration avec l'équipe Building2050.

En tant que volet intégré de la thèse de doctorat, le candidat appliquera et adaptera le cadre REGEN4BE à certains systèmes de logement à base de blocs de terre et de ciment calcaire calciné (LC3) dans des contextes africains. S'appuyant sur les projets et les partenariats SONO, cette recherche examinera comment les matériaux locaux, les stratégies environnementales passives, les processus de construction, le carbone tout-terrain, la circularité, la réparabilité, la performance mesurée des bâtiments et l'expérience des résidents peuvent éclairer la conception régénératrice.

Les volets de recherche européen et africain formeront un projet de doctorat cohérent. Le candidat contribuera à un cadre générique d'interopérabilité au sein de REGEN4BE et évaluera sa transférabilité et l'adaptation nécessaire à différents matériaux, climats, cultures de construction et niveaux d'infrastructure numérique.

Principales fonctions et responsabilités

En tant qu'étudiant en doctorat, vous assumerez la responsabilité scientifique d'élaborer et de terminer votre thèse de doctorat, de formuler des questions de recherche originales et d'établir une méthodologie rigoureuse. Vous effectuerez des recherches informatiques, expérimentales et sur le terrain en collaboration avec des partenaires universitaires, techniques, institutionnels, de développement de logiciels et de l'industrie. Vos responsabilités comprendront la collecte, la gestion, l'analyse et l'interprétation de données quantitatives et qualitatives, la préparation d'articles pour des revues évaluées par les pairs, la présentation de conclusions lors de conférences, d'ateliers et de réunions de projets, la contribution aux produits livrables REGEN4BE, les démonstrations et les activités de diffusion, la participation à l'enseignement et, le cas échéant, la supervision de projets étudiants.

Au sein de REGEN4BE, vous contribuerez au développement et à la validation scientifique de la plateforme d'intelligence de conception régénératrice (REDIP) et de ses workflows de construction-données et d'évaluation des performances. Vous développerez et testerez des méthodes interopérables reliant BIM, openBIM et IFC avec des modèles building-energy, Life-Cycle Assessment, des calculs de carbone sur toute la vie, des indicateurs de circularité, des données de surveillance, la rétroaction des occupants et l'évaluation post-occupation. Vous étudierez la continuité des données, la traçabilité, l'incertitude et l'interopérabilité au cours des phases de conception, de construction et d'exploitation des bâtiments, et définirez les exigences en matière d'information et les structures de données pour l'échange de géométrie, de matériaux, d'indicateurs environnementaux, de performances mesurées et de rétroaction des occupants dans les environnements numériques.

Vous établirez des protocoles pour évaluer la fiabilité, l'exactitude, l'exhaustivité, la reproductibilité et la convivialité des workflows proposés. En utilisant les ensembles de données et l'infrastructure Smart Living Lab, vous effectuerez des essais à grande échelle, la collecte de données, l'étalonnage des modèles et la validation scientifique à Fribourg. Vous comparerez les performances prévues et simulées avec les conditions environnementales mesurées et l'expérience des occupants, et collaborerez avec Building2050, les laboratoires pertinents de l'EPFL et les plateformes de recherche ENAC, y compris PL-MTI le cas échéant. Vous soutiendrez également les spécifications scientifiques, les essais et la validation des API, connecteurs, pipelines de données et interfaces en coordination avec les partenaires de développement logiciel du projet, et évaluerez la transférabilité des méthodes à travers les sites de démonstration REGEN4BE et différents contextes de construction, climatiques et institutionnels.

Dans le cadre de la thèse de doctorat, vous appliquerez et adapterez le cadre REGEN4BE à certains projets et partenariats SONO en Afrique. Vous développerez des structures d'information BIM pour les blocs de terre, les systèmes de terre comprimée et stabilisée, les blocs à base de LC3, les mortiers, les composants en béton et les assemblages connexes, intégrant des données de matériaux et de construction spécifiques localement. Vous étudierez les workflows BIM-to-BEM pour la performance environnementale passive, y compris la masse thermique, la protection solaire, la ventilation naturelle, le mouvement de l'air intérieur, la température, l'humidité et les ouvertures contrôlées par les occupants. Vous développerez également des LCA, du carbone tout-vivant et des méthodes circulaires pour les constructions locales, à faible teneur en carbone et réparables, déterminerez quelles méthodes sont transférables et qui nécessitent une adaptation aux conditions climatiques, matérielles, économiques, techniques et sociales locales, et traduireez les résultats en recommandations de conception et en méthodes d'aide à la décision pour les logements régénératifs et respectueux du climat.

Profil

• Maîtrise en architecture, ingénierie architecturale, sciences du bâtiment, génie civil, génie mécanique, conception informatique, ingénierie environnementale ou domaine connexe

• Fort intérêt pour l'intersection de la conception architecturale, de la technologie du bâtiment, de la performance environnementale et des méthodes numériques

• Expérience des flux de travail BIM et intérêt pour des environnements numériques ouverts et interopérables, y compris IFC

• Connaissances ou expérience dans un ou plusieurs des domaines suivants :
- modélisation et simulation de l'énergie du bâtiment;
- Évaluation du cycle de vie;
- évaluation du carbone incorporé et opérationnel;
- construction circulaire;
- la surveillance des bâtiments et l'évaluation après l'occupation;
- la conception informatique;
- interopérabilité des données de construction

• Fortes compétences en analyse de données et capacité de travailler avec des ensembles de données hétérogènes provenant de modèles numériques, de simulations, de bases de données environnementales, de capteurs, d'enquêtes et d'entrevues

• Expérience dans la programmation scientifique, le script ou l'automatisation du workflow. La connaissance du python ou d'une langue équivalente est hautement souhaitable

• L'expérience avec les API, les bases de données, la programmation visuelle, la conception paramétrique ou la visualisation des données est un atout.
Intérêt pour la construction de la terre, les systèmes cimentaires à faible teneur en carbone, la LC3, la conception environnementale passive et le logement dans les contextes africains

• Intérêt pour l'expérimentation à grande échelle, Living Labs, et les liens entre la recherche, la conception, la construction, l'exploitation du bâtiment et l'expérience des occupants

• Capacité de mener des travaux sur le terrain et de collaborer avec des chercheurs, des professionnels, des entrepreneurs, des établissements, des collectivités et des résidents

• Capacité de formuler des questions de recherche originales, d'élaborer des méthodes de validation rigoureuses et de communiquer les résultats au moyen de publications scientifiques évaluées par les pairs

• Excellent anglais écrit et parlé; le français est un atout

• L'autonomie scientifique, la curiosité intellectuelle et la capacité de travailler efficacement dans un environnement de recherche interdisciplinaire et international.

Nous offrons

• Quatre ans pour compléter votre doctorat, avec une rémunération compétitive selon les conditions d'emploi de l'EPFL

• Une occasion de développer un profil scientifique distinct à l'intersection de la conception régénératrice, de l'interopérabilité des données sur le bâtiment, de la simulation environnementale, de l'évaluation du carbone tout-terrain, de la construction circulaire, de la surveillance du bâtiment et des matériaux à faible teneur en carbone

• Participation à un grand consortium international Horizon Europe impliquant des partenaires académiques, publics, techniques, de conception et industriels

Informations

Le doctorant sera basé au Laboratoire Sud-Nord pour la Construction et la Conservation Durables, au sein de l'EPFL School of Architecture, Civil and Environmental Engineering, au campus associé à l'EPFL Fribourg. La thèse sera supervisée par le Prof. Aziza Chaouni.

Documents de demande

Les demandes doivent comprendre :

Veuillez ne pas télécharger de lettres de référence avec la demande de recrutement. Seuls les noms et les coordonnées des arbitres sont requis à ce stade. Ils peuvent ensuite être contactés directement par le gestionnaire d'embauche. La demande distincte EDAR suit sa propre procédure de recommandation confidentielle.

jobs.description:
Mission

Understanding how urban sustainability transitions interact: How do transformations in different urban sectors—such as energy and food—interact? Under what conditions do they reinforce one another or create trade-offs, and when do they trigger tipping dynamics?

The Laboratory for Human-Environment Relations in Urban Systems (HERUS) at the School of Architecture, Civil and Environmental Engineering (ENAC), EPFL, investigates how urban systems transform towards sustainability. We are looking for a PhD candidate to investigate coupled sustainability transitions, with an initial focus on the interactions between energy and food systems.

The PhD project is embedded within the ongoing research project “Tipping Transition”, which investigates the drivers and dynamics of renewable energy technology adoption in housing in Lausanne. An interdisciplinary agent-based model (ABM) has been developed to represent the energy transition at the level of Lausanne, integrating not only economic factors but also social and behavioural dimensions, such as attitudes, social norm, and their evolution over time.

The PhD project “Trade-off and tipping dynamics in urban transitions “ will extend this modelling framework to investigate interactions between different urban sectors, initially focusing on energy and food. A particular focus will be placed on the role of provisioning systems—the infrastructures, technologies, institutions, markets, and practices through which goods and services are provided—in enabling or constraining sustainability transitions.

The successful candidate will work in collaboration with a current PhD researcher developing the energy transition model. This provides an opportunity to build on an established modelling framework, contribute to its further development, and benefit from expertise and ongoing research.

Main duties and responsibilities

• Develop a framework for analyzing coupled sustainability transitions in urban systems.

• Extend and further develop an interdisciplinary agent-based model of urban transitions in Lausanne.

• Investigate synergies, trade-offs, and tipping dynamics between sectors such as energy and food.

• Analyse how changes in provisioning systems influence sustainability transitions

• Develop and conduct your own research under the guidance of Prof. Claudia R. Binder.

• Collaborate closely with the HERUS research team and the existing PhD project.

• Publish research findings in international peer-reviewed journals and present them at scientific conferences.

• Contribute to teaching and student supervision at EPFL (20%).

Profile

• An excellent MSc degree in Computer Science, Energy Science, Social Sciences, Environmental Sciences, Sustainability Science, Geography, or a closely related interdiscipline.

• A strong interest in sustainability transitions and/or urban systems tipping dynamics.

• Good knowledge of computational modelling and programming. Experience with Python and agent-based modelling is particularly valuable. Knowledge of Scala or Julia is an asset.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills and an interest in interdisciplinary research.

• Strong communication and interpersonal skills, the ability to work independently, and a high level of motivation for academic research.

• Excellent written and spoken English. Knowledge of French and/or German is an asset.

Previous experience with agent-based modelling or sustainability transitions is welcome, but candidates with a strong quantitative or computational background and an interest in developing interdisciplinary expertise are also encouraged to apply.

We offer

• A PhD position for up to four years within an interdisciplinary and international research environment at EPFL.

• The opportunity to develop an independent research profile at the intersection of computational modelling, sustainability science, and urban studies.

• Close collaboration with the HERUS research team.

• The opportunity to contribute to the development of innovative approaches for understanding interconnected urban sustainability transitions.

• Structured doctoral training through EPFL doctoral programs and close research mentorship.

Informations

The selection process involves multiple stages, and short-listed candidates will be requested to apply to a specific EPFL Doctoral Program to qualify for a PhD at EPFL, i.e. EDCE.
Please check this page for additional information on admission.

Please note that this is a separate application process necessary to be eligible to complete your PhD at EPFL.

Your application should contain:

• Motivation letter: A statement (max. one page), where you outline why you want to join this group, what your specific interests are, how your skills can contribute to the mission of the HERUS laboratory and how you think you can advance in your own academic/scholarly pursuit while being a part of the team.

• Detailed CV

• Contact information

• The names and contact information of 3 references

• Transcript of records (Bachelor and Master)

Application deadline: 12/11/2026

Contract Start Date: 02/01/2027

Activity Rate: 100.00

Contract Type: CDD

Duration: 4 years

Reference: 2503

For inquiries regarding the position and project scope, please contact Prof. Claudia R. Binder ( claudia.binder@epfl.ch ) or Dr. Maria Anna Hecher ( maria.hecher@epfl.ch ).

For more information on past and ongoing research at HERUS, please visit: http://herus.epfl.ch/

descriptionByLocale.it:
Missione

Comprendere come interagiscono le transizioni della sostenibilità urbana: come interagiscono le trasformazioni in diversi settori urbani, come l'energia e il cibo? In quali condizioni si rafforzano l'un l'altro o creano trade-off, e quando innescano dinamiche di ribaltamento?

Il Laboratorio per le relazioni umane in sistemi urbani (HERUS) presso la Scuola di Architettura, Ingegneria Civile e Ambientale (ENAC), EPFL, indaga su come i sistemi urbani si trasformano verso la sostenibilità. Stiamo cercando un Dottorato di Ricerca per indagare le transizioni di sostenibilità accoppiate, con un primo focus sulle interazioni tra energia e sistemi alimentari.

Il progetto PhD è incorporato all’interno del progetto di ricerca in corso “Tipping Transition”, che indaga i driver e le dinamiche dell’adozione di tecnologie energetiche rinnovabili nell’edilizia abitativa a Losanna. Un modello basato sull'agente interdisciplinare (ABM) è stato sviluppato per rappresentare la transizione energetica a livello di Losanna, integrando non solo fattori economici, ma anche dimensioni sociali e comportamentali, come atteggiamenti, norma sociale, e la loro evoluzione nel tempo.

Il progetto PhD “Trade-off e ribaltamento dinamica nelle transizioni urbane” estenderà questo quadro di modellazione per indagare le interazioni tra diversi settori urbani, inizialmente concentrandosi sull’energia e sul cibo. Una particolare attenzione sarà posta sul ruolo dei sistemi di provisioning, le infrastrutture, le tecnologie, le istituzioni, i mercati e le pratiche attraverso le quali vengono forniti beni e servizi, consentendo o ostacolando le transizioni di sostenibilità.

Il candidato di successo lavorerà in collaborazione con un attuale ricercatore di dottorato che sviluppa il modello di transizione energetica. Questo offre l'opportunità di costruire su un quadro di modellazione consolidato, contribuire al suo ulteriore sviluppo, e beneficiare di competenze e ricerche in corso.

Principali doveri e responsabilità

• Sviluppare un quadro per analizzare le transizioni di sostenibilità accoppiate nei sistemi urbani.

• Estendere e sviluppare ulteriormente un modello interdisciplinare di transizioni urbane a Losanna.

• Investigare sinergie, trade-off e ribaltare le dinamiche tra settori come l'energia e il cibo.

• Analizzare come i cambiamenti nei sistemi di provisioning influenzano le transizioni di sostenibilità

• Sviluppare e condurre la propria ricerca sotto la guida del Prof. Claudia R. Binder.

• Collabora a stretto contatto con il team di ricerca HERUS e con il progetto PhD esistente.

• Pubblicare i risultati della ricerca in riviste peer-reviewed internazionali e presentarli a conferenze scientifiche.

• Contribuire all'insegnamento e alla supervisione degli studenti all'EPFL (20%).

Profilo

• Un eccellente MSc laurea in Informatica, Scienza dell'Energia, Scienze sociali, Scienze Ambientali, Scienza della Sostenibilità, Geografia, o una stretta interdisciplinare.

• Un forte interesse per le transizioni di sostenibilità e/o i sistemi urbani che ribaltano le dinamiche.

• Buona conoscenza della modellazione computazionale e della programmazione. L'esperienza con Python e la modellazione basata sugli agenti è particolarmente preziosa. La conoscenza della Scala o di Julia è una risorsa.

• Forte capacità analitiche e di problem solving e un interesse per la ricerca interdisciplinare.

• Forte comunicazione e competenze interpersonali, la capacità di lavorare in modo indipendente, e un alto livello di motivazione per la ricerca accademica.

• Ottimo scritto e parlato inglese. La conoscenza del francese e/o del tedesco è un bene.

L'esperienza precedente con modellizzazione basata su agenti o transizioni di sostenibilità è gradita, ma i candidati con un forte background quantitativo o computazionale e un interesse per lo sviluppo di competenze interdisciplinari sono anche incoraggiati ad applicare.

Offriamo

• Una posizione di dottorato fino a quattro anni all'interno di un ambiente di ricerca interdisciplinare e internazionale all'EPFL.

• L'opportunità di sviluppare un profilo di ricerca indipendente all'incrocio tra modellismo computazionale, scienza della sostenibilità e studi urbani.

• Una stretta collaborazione con il team di ricerca HERUS.

• L'opportunità di contribuire allo sviluppo di approcci innovativi per comprendere transizioni interconnesse di sostenibilità urbana.

• Formazione di dottorato strutturata attraverso programmi di dottorato EPFL e una stretta mentorship di ricerca.

Informazioni

Il processo di selezione coinvolge più fasi, e candidati a lista corta sarà richiesto di applicare a un programma specifico di dottorato EPFL per qualificarsi per un dottorato in EPFL, cioè EDCE.
Si prega di controllare questa pagina per ulteriori informazioni sull'ammissione.

Si prega di notare che questo è un processo di applicazione separato necessario per essere idonei a completare il dottorato in EPFL.

La tua domanda dovrebbe contenere:

• Lettera di motivazione: Una dichiarazione (max. una pagina), dove si delinea il motivo per cui si desidera aderire a questo gruppo, quali sono i vostri interessi specifici, come le vostre competenze possono contribuire alla missione del laboratorio HERUS e come si pensa di poter avanzare nella vostra propria ricerca accademica/scholarly mentre fanno parte della squadra.

• CV dettagliato

• Informazioni di contatto

• I nomi e le informazioni di contatto di 3 riferimenti

• Trascrizione di record (Bachelor e Master)

Termine per la richiesta: 12/11/20

Data di inizio del contratto: 02/01/2027

Tasso di attività: 100.00

Tipo di contratto: CDD

Durata: 4 anni

Riferimento: 2503

Per domande relative alla posizione e alla portata del progetto, si prega di contattare il Prof. Claudia R. Binder ( claudia.binder@epfl.ch ) o il Dott. Maria Anna Hecher ( maria.hecher@epfl.ch ).

Per ulteriori informazioni sulle ricerche passate e in corso presso HERUS, visitare il sito: http://herus.epfl.ch/

descriptionByLocale.de:
Mission

Verstehen, wie urbane Nachhaltigkeitsübergänge interagieren: Wie interagieren Transformationen in verschiedenen städtischen Sektoren wie Energie und Nahrung? Unter welchen Bedingungen verstärken sie sich gegenseitig oder schaffen Kompromisse und wann lösen sie Kippdynamiken aus?

Das Laboratory for Human-Environment Relations in Urban Systems (HERUS) an der School of Architecture, Civil and Environmental Engineering (ENAC), EPFL, untersucht, wie sich urbane Systeme in Richtung Nachhaltigkeit wandeln. Wir suchen einen Doktoranden, der gekoppelte Nachhaltigkeitsübergänge untersucht, wobei der Schwerpunkt zunächst auf den Wechselwirkungen zwischen Energie- und Lebensmittelsystemen liegt.

Das PhD-Projekt ist eingebettet in das laufende Forschungsprojekt „Tipping Transition, das die Treiber und Dynamiken der Einführung erneuerbarer Energietechnologien im Wohnungsbau in Lausanne untersucht. Ein interdisziplinäres agentenbasiertes Modell (ABM) wurde entwickelt, um die Energiewende auf Lausanner Ebene darzustellen und nicht nur wirtschaftliche Faktoren, sondern auch soziale und verhaltensbezogene Dimensionen wie Einstellungen, soziale Norm und ihre Entwicklung im Laufe der Zeit zu integrieren.

Das PhD-Projekt „Trade-off and tipping dynamics in urban transitions wird diesen Modellierungsrahmen erweitern, um Wechselwirkungen zwischen verschiedenen städtischen Sektoren zu untersuchen, wobei zunächst der Schwerpunkt auf Energie und Nahrung liegt. Ein besonderer Schwerpunkt liegt auf der Rolle von Bereitstellungssystemen - den Infrastrukturen, Technologien, Institutionen, Märkten und Praktiken, durch die Waren und Dienstleistungen bereitgestellt werden - bei der Ermöglichung oder Einschränkung von Nachhaltigkeitsübergängen.

Der erfolgreiche Kandidat wird in Zusammenarbeit mit einem aktuellen Doktoranden arbeiten, der das Energiewendemodell entwickelt. Dies bietet die Möglichkeit, auf einem etablierten Modellierungsrahmen aufzubauen, zu seiner Weiterentwicklung beizutragen und von Fachwissen und laufender Forschung zu profitieren.

Hauptaufgaben und Zuständigkeiten

• Entwicklung eines Rahmens zur Analyse gekoppelter Nachhaltigkeitsübergänge in städtischen Systemen.

• Ausbau und Weiterentwicklung eines interdisziplinären agentenbasierten Modells urbaner Transitionen in Lausanne.

• Untersuchen Sie Synergien, Kompromisse und Kippdynamiken zwischen Sektoren wie Energie und Lebensmittel.

• Analysieren Sie, wie Änderungen in Bereitstellungssystemen Nachhaltigkeitsübergänge beeinflussen

• Entwickeln und betreiben Sie Ihre eigene Forschung unter der Leitung von Prof. Claudia R. Binder.

• Enge Zusammenarbeit mit dem HERUS-Forschungsteam und dem bestehenden PhD-Projekt.

• Veröffentlichen Sie Forschungsergebnisse in internationalen Fachzeitschriften und präsentieren Sie sie auf wissenschaftlichen Konferenzen.

• Beitrag zur Lehre und Betreuung der Studierenden an der EPFL (20%).

Profil

• Ein ausgezeichneter MSc-Abschluss in Informatik, Energiewissenschaft, Sozialwissenschaften, Umweltwissenschaften, Nachhaltigkeitswissenschaft, Geographie oder einer eng verwandten Interdisziplinarität.

• Ein starkes Interesse an Nachhaltigkeitsübergängen und / oder urbanen Systemen, die die Dynamik verändern.

• Gute Kenntnisse der Computermodellierung und Programmierung. Erfahrung mit Python und agentenbasierter Modellierung ist besonders wertvoll. Kenntnisse von Scala oder Julia sind ein Gewinn.

• Starke analytische und problemlösende Fähigkeiten und Interesse an interdisziplinärer Forschung.

• Starke Kommunikation und zwischenmenschliche Fähigkeiten, die Fähigkeit, unabhängig zu arbeiten, und ein hohes Maß an Motivation für die akademische Forschung.

• Hervorragend geschriebenes und gesprochenes Englisch. Französisch und/oder Deutschkenntnisse sind ein Gewinn.

Frühere Erfahrungen mit agentenbasierten Modellen oder Nachhaltigkeitsübergängen sind willkommen, aber auch Kandidaten mit einem starken quantitativen oder rechnerischen Hintergrund und einem Interesse an der Entwicklung interdisziplinärer Expertise werden ermutigt, sich zu bewerben.

descriptionByLocale.fr:
Mission

Comprendre comment interagissent les transitions vers la durabilité urbaine : comment interagissent les transformations dans différents secteurs urbains, comme l'énergie et l'alimentation ? Dans quelles conditions se renforcent-ils ou créent-ils des compromis, et quand déclenchent-ils une dynamique de basculement?

Le Laboratoire pour les relations entre l'homme et l'environnement dans les systèmes urbains (HERUS) de l'École d'architecture, d'ingénierie civile et environnementale (ENAC), EPFL, étudie comment les systèmes urbains se transforment en durabilité. Nous sommes à la recherche d'un candidat au doctorat pour étudier les transitions de durabilité couplées, avec un accent initial sur les interactions entre l'énergie et les systèmes alimentaires.

Le projet de doctorat est intégré dans le projet de recherche en cours «Tipping Transition», qui étudie les moteurs et la dynamique de l'adoption de technologies d'énergie renouvelable dans le logement à Lausanne. Un modèle interdisciplinaire basé sur les agents (ABM) a été développé pour représenter la transition énergétique au niveau de Lausanne, intégrant non seulement des facteurs économiques mais aussi des dimensions sociales et comportementales telles que les attitudes, les normes sociales et leur évolution au fil du temps.

Le projet doctorant "Trade-off et la dynamique de basculement dans les transitions urbaines" étendra ce cadre de modélisation pour étudier les interactions entre les différents secteurs urbains, en se concentrant initialement sur l'énergie et l'alimentation. L'accent sera mis en particulier sur le rôle de la fourniture de systèmes — les infrastructures, les technologies, les institutions, les marchés et les pratiques par le biais desquels les biens et les services sont fournis — pour permettre ou limiter les transitions vers la durabilité.

Le candidat retenu travaillera en collaboration avec un doctorant actuel qui élaborera le modèle de transition énergétique. Cela offre l'occasion de s'appuyer sur un cadre de modélisation établi, de contribuer à son perfectionnement et de bénéficier de l'expertise et de la recherche continue.

Principales fonctions et responsabilités

• Élaborer un cadre pour l'analyse des transitions de durabilité couplées dans les systèmes urbains.

• Étendre et développer un modèle interdisciplinaire de transition urbaine basé sur les agents à Lausanne.

• Étudier les synergies, les compromis et la dynamique de basculement entre des secteurs comme l'énergie et l'alimentation.

• Analyser comment l'évolution des systèmes d'approvisionnement influe sur les transitions vers la durabilité

• Développer et mener vos propres recherches sous la direction de la Prof. Claudia R. Binder.

• Collaborer étroitement avec l'équipe de recherche HERUS et le projet de doctorat existant.

• Publier les résultats de la recherche dans des revues internationales évaluées par des pairs et les présenter lors de conférences scientifiques.

• Contribuer à l'enseignement et à la supervision étudiante à l'EPFL (20 %).

Profil

• Excellente maîtrise en informatique, sciences de l'énergie, sciences sociales, sciences de l'environnement, sciences de la durabilité, géographie ou une interdiscipline étroitement liée.

• Un fort intérêt pour les transitions durables et/ou la dynamique de basculement des systèmes urbains.

• Bonne connaissance de la modélisation et de la programmation informatiques. L'expérience du Python et de la modélisation par agents est particulièrement précieuse. La connaissance de Scala ou Julia est un atout.

• Forte capacité d'analyse et de résolution de problèmes et intérêt pour la recherche interdisciplinaire.

• De solides compétences en communication et en relations interpersonnelles, la capacité de travailler de façon indépendante et un niveau élevé de motivation pour la recherche universitaire.

• Excellent écrit et parlé anglais. La connaissance du français et/ou de l'allemand est un atout.

Une expérience antérieure de la modélisation basée sur les agents ou des transitions de durabilité est bienvenue, mais les candidats ayant une solide expérience quantitative ou computationnelle et un intérêt pour le développement d'une expertise interdisciplinaire sont également encouragés à postuler.

Nous offrons

• Un doctorat de quatre ans au sein d'un environnement de recherche interdisciplinaire et international à l'EPFL.

• L'occasion d'élaborer un profil de recherche indépendant à l'intersection de la modélisation computationnelle, de la science de la durabilité et des études urbaines.

• Collaboration étroite avec l'équipe de recherche HERUS.

• L'occasion de contribuer à l'élaboration d'approches novatrices pour comprendre les transitions interdépendantes en matière de durabilité urbaine.

• Formation doctorale structurée grâce à des programmes de doctorat de l'EPFL et à un mentorat de recherche étroit.

Informations

Le processus de sélection comporte plusieurs étapes, et les candidats présélectionnés seront invités à postuler à un programme de doctorat spécifique de l'EPFL pour obtenir un doctorat à l'EPFL, c'est-à-dire l'EDCE.
Veuillez consulter cette page pour plus d'informations sur l'admission.

Veuillez noter qu'il s'agit d'un processus de candidature séparé nécessaire pour être éligible pour compléter votre doctorat à l'EPFL.

Votre demande doit contenir :

• Lettre de motivation: Une déclaration (max. une page), où vous expliquez pourquoi vous voulez rejoindre ce groupe, quels sont vos intérêts spécifiques, comment vos compétences peuvent contribuer à la mission du laboratoire HERUS et comment vous pensez pouvoir progresser dans votre propre poursuite académique/scolaire tout en faisant partie de l'équipe.

• CV détaillé

• Coordonnées

• Noms et coordonnées de 3 références

• Transcription des dossiers (Bachelor et Master)
